title: A hawkish US Fed and heavy debt supply raise the rates bar
gist: Oxford Economics raises its rate forecasts for a more hawkish Fed and higher neutral rate, sees the AI buildout offsetting rate drag but raising downside risk, and flags stocks, private credit and small business as key vulnerabilities.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics raised its October interest-rate forecasts to reflect a more hawkish Fed, a higher neutral rate and elevated inflation risks.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Baseline rates path is higher; revisit duration and funding-cost assumptions.

insights.claim: The AI buildout is offsetting the economic drag from higher rates, which raises the probability of downside risks, with the stock market, private credit and small business the three key vulnerabilities.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Track these three channels for where rate stress emerges first.

insights.claim: Long-end yield pressure is compounded by geopolitical uncertainty, growing sovereign and AI-led corporate debt issuance, a shifting base of Treasury buyers and weaker demand at Treasury auctions.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Supply and demand technicals favour a steeper, higher long end.

insights.claim: Yield risks hinge on energy prices: persistent oil shocks or weaker Treasury demand push yields higher, while faster oil declines or an AI-led market correction would pull them down sooner.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Oil and an AI correction are the swing factors for yields.
